description: Fix Proton 'Cannot find graph for graphExecId' warning by starting Proton session before CUDA graph capture and deactivating after capture completes

userStories.title: Add start_and_deactivate method to ProtonProfilerWrapper
userStories.description: As a developer, I want ProtonProfilerWrapper to support creating a session and later deactivating it so that the GPU worker can start Proton before CUDA graph capture and deactivate after capture completes.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a public method start_and_deactivate() to ProtonProfilerWrapper in vllm/profiler/wrapper.py
start_and_deactivate() calls _create_session() to create the Proton session via proton.start()
start_and_deactivate() does NOT immediately deactivate — the caller controls when to deactivate
Add a public method deactivate_early() that calls proton.deactivate() WITHOUT flushing to pause the session
After start_and_deactivate() + deactivate_early(), internal state has _session_id set and _running is False
Subsequent calls to _start() detect existing _session_id and call proton.activate() instead of proton.start() (for both periodic and non-periodic modes)
In non-periodic mode, _stop() after an activate()-based start calls proton.deactivate(flushing=True) then proton.finalize(), not just proton.finalize()
Unit tests cover: start_and_deactivate then deactivate_early then _start activates existing session then _stop finalizes
Unit tests cover: both periodic and non-periodic modes work correctly with the early-start pattern
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: This is the core wrapper change. The two-method split (start_and_deactivate + deactivate_early) lets the GPU worker keep Proton active during CUDA graph capture and deactivate only after capture completes.

userStories.title: Wire early Proton start in GPU worker compile_or_warm_up_model
userStories.description: As a developer profiling vLLM with Proton, I want the Proton session started before CUDA graph capture and deactivated after capture so that Proton tracks graph creation without the 'Cannot find graph' warning.
acceptanceCriteria: In gpu_worker.py compile_or_warm_up_model(), when profiler_config.profiler == 'proton', create ProtonProfilerWrapper and call start_and_deactivate() BEFORE capture_model() is called
Call deactivate_early() AFTER capture_model() returns — Proton is active during the entire CUDA graph capture phase
Store the wrapper in self.profiler so profile(is_start=True) reuses it via the existing 'if self.profiler is None' guard
Only Proton profiler gets early initialization — torch and cuda profiler types are unaffected
When enforce_eager is True (no CUDA graph capture), still start and deactivate Proton early for consistency
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-001. Key sequence: proton.start() → warmup + capture_model() → proton.deactivate(). The existing profile() method already guards with 'if self.profiler is None' so it will reuse the early-created wrapper.

userStories.title: Ensure profile() reuses early-initialized Proton profiler correctly
userStories.description: As a developer, I want profile(is_start=True) to correctly activate the deactivated Proton session created during init rather than creating a duplicate.
acceptanceCriteria: profile(is_start=True) skips wrapper creation when self.profiler is not None (existing guard at line 776)
profile(is_start=True) calls self.profiler.start() which internally calls proton.activate() on the existing deactivated session
profile(is_start=False) calls self.profiler.stop() which works correctly whether session was early-started or not
Both periodic and non-periodic Proton modes work correctly: start_profile → generate → stop_profile cycle produces valid output
Unit tests verify the full lifecycle: early init in compile_or_warm_up_model → start_profile → stop_profile
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-001 and US-002. This story verifies the integration between early init and the existing profile() API. The existing 'if self.profiler is None' guard should handle this naturally.

userStories.title: Verify fix with vllm_offline.sh end-to-end
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to run the offline profiling script and confirm the Proton warning is eliminated and valid profiles are produced.
acceptanceCriteria: Run scripts/profiling/vllm_offline.sh end-to-end (or sanity_check.sh with a small model)
No '[PROTON] Cannot find graph for graphExecId' warning in output
Valid .hatchet output files are produced and loadable by proton-viewer
Profile output includes CUDA graph capture activity (visible in proton-viewer output)
userStories.notes: Depends on US-002 and US-003. This is a manual verification story — run the actual profiling script and check output.
